subject: Renewal pricing & short-term capacity uplift request
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Bowman <alex@clearviewlabs.com>, Clearview Procurement <procurement@clearviewlabs.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing & short-term capacity uplift request

Hi Alex — looping in procurement per your previous thread.

Clearview's current annual term is up at the end of June and I wanted to start a quick, focused conversation about renewal economics and a short-term capacity uplift you mentioned on the last call.

A couple of items I want to understand so I can put options on the table:
- Expected Q3 run-rate growth (rough ballpark % over current usage).
- Whether you need a temporary burst credit pool versus a permanent committed uplift.
- Procurement timelines / PO window if we can agree commercial.

We have a few practical levers we can use: modest renewal discount, time-bound credit buckets to cover bursts, or a price-hold for 12 months paired with a firm commit increase. I can draft two clean options for procurement once I know the above.

Can we do a 30-minute call early next week? If procurement prefers, I can include a draft term sheet for review ahead of the call (I attached an internal draft to speed things up).

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Clearview_Q2_usage_summary.csv (summary export), Clearview_Renewal_TermSheet_v2.pdf (draft)
From: Alex Bowman <alex@clearviewlabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Clearview Procurement <procurement@clearviewlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing & short-term capacity uplift request

Thanks Sergio — appreciate the heads up. Short answers:
- We expect ~30% uplift in token volume for Q3 tied to a new pilot (likely sustained at 10-15% thereafter).
- Procurement would prefer a time-bound credit bucket to avoid a permanent rebase right away. They also asked about an interim price-hold while we evaluate the pilot.
- Ideally we can get a PO signed by June 15 if the commercial looks reasonable.

High level ask from procurement (copied): Is Redwood willing to provide a 12‑month price-hold on current rates plus a temporary credit pool (~$50k) to cover the Q3 pilot burst? If not, what's the delta to reserve 30% more capacity immediately?

Can you propose 1-2 concrete options? Procurement will need line-item clarity to move a PO.

—Alex
Head of Product | Clearview Labs
alex@clearviewlabs.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Bowman <alex@clearviewlabs.com>, Clearview Procurement <procurement@clearviewlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal pricing & short-term capacity uplift request

Marissa / Priyom — forwarding Clearview's request. They want a 12‑month price‑hold OR a small renewal discount + a $50k temporary credit pool to cover a Q3 30% spike. Procurement needs PO by 6/15.

Draft options I had in mind:
A) Price-hold: 12 months at current rates, commit stays flat. No credits. They get priority burst routing but pay overage at existing rates.
B) Discount + credits: 10% off renewal rate (12‑month term) + $50k one‑time credit bucket applied to Q3 overages. We can require PO by 6/15 and include a 90‑day review to convert credits into a permanent uplift if usage remains high.

I attached the draft term sheet (v2) and Q2 usage so you can see the baseline. Need final guidance on whether 10% + $50k credit is acceptable or whether to hold firm and offer a different structure.

If we push further (20% or larger credit) we should flag to leadership.

—Sergio
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Bowman <alex@clearviewlabs.com>, Clearview Procurement <procurement@clearviewlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal pricing & short-term capacity uplift request

Sergio — good summary. I think we can land this without escalation. Proposed commercial (Option B, clean):
- Term: 12 months starting on signature.
- Renewal discount: 10% off list for the first 12‑month renewal term.
- Credit pool: $50,000 one‑time credit (applied to overage/burst charges) valid for usage between Jul 1 — Sep 30, 2028. Unused credits expire after Sept 30.
- PO requirement: PO or signed SOW by June 15 for activation of credits.
- Operational: Automatic priority routing for burst traffic up to the credit amount; overage beyond credits billed at the discounted rate.

Rationale: 10% + $50k protects their Q3 pilot runway and preserves long‑term economics. If usage stays elevated we can convert credits into an uplifted commit during the 90‑day review and reconcile billing.

I attached a clean term sheet reflecting the above (Clearview_Renewal_TermSheet_v2.pdf). If procurement pushes for a price‑hold instead of a discount, we should ask for a 6‑month firm PO/commit to justify holding list rates.

If you get procurement on the phone, confirm they can do PO by 6/15 and I'll prep DocuSign.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal pricing & short-term capacity uplift request

Quick operational note from infra/ops:
- We can provision an additional 30% capacity as a burst pool; cost to Redwood to reserve the capacity short term is roughly equivalent to a 12% uplift on their committed template if they wanted permanent capacity.
- If we implement Marissa's Option B (credits + 10% discount) we should configure the credit as a prepaid billing adjustment rather than a retroactive rebate to simplify procurement.
- I'll attach a short ops appendix (not legal) outlining routing priority and expected provisioning lead time (usually 48–72 hours for dedicated routing).

I'll stand by to confirm provisioning once procurement signals PO intent.

—Priyom Das
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal pricing & short-term capacity uplift request

Team — thanks, this looks workable. Clearview will accept Option B as written: 10% renewal discount + $50k credit pool valid Jul–Sep 2028. Procurement intends to issue a PO by June 14.

Can you send a revised term sheet and a DocuSign link for signature? Also please confirm provisioning timeline once PO is issued so we can coordinate the pilot launch.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
